Nested APs inherit the active runtime. <p dir="auto">ramure is an opinionated and lightweight Python library for building reliable agent software. It makes it easy to define programs where agents communicate across environments to accomplish a task.</p>
<p dir="auto">Making agent software (software that calls agents) is a complex distributed systems problem. The goal of ramure is to make it easier to build and robustify these systems, in 2 notable ways:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Infrastructure primitives</strong>: for agent communication, provisioning, and the software environments in which they run</li>
<li><strong>Fault-tolerant and modular design</strong>: ramure's  abstractions and event based logic make it easier to write agents that fail loudly and retry using ideas from distributed systems programming like Erlang. See <a href="https://fulcrum.inc/2026/04/30/multi-agent-as-distributed.html" rel="nofollow">multi-agent systems as distributed software</a> for the motivation behind ramure's design.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Here are some examples of tasks ramure makes easy with agents:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>optimization</li>
<li>custom software generation pipelines with user input</li>
<li>data pipelines</li>
<li>worker pools, monitors, and supervisors</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Note: ramure is the successor to our earlier agent runtime druids. The old code is preserved at <a href="https://github.com/fulcrumresearch/druids-archive">fulcrumresearch/druids-archive</a>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Here is an annotated single worker program:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="import asyncio
from ramure import agent, agent_process, done, fail, wait

# registers the ramure runtime which will manage the agents and their machines, as well as controlling the lifecycle/cleanup
@agent_process
async def run_task(spec: str) -> str:
    # initialize an agent (either locally or on a remote sandbox)
    worker = await agent(f"worker")

    # register tools the agent can call in-harness
    @worker.on("finish")
    async def on_finish(summary: str) -> str:
        """Call with your result when the task is done."""
        done(summary)
        return "Recorded."

    @worker.on("give_up")
    async def on_give_up(reason: str) -> str:
        """Call if you cannot complete the task."""
        fail(f"gave_up: {reason}")
        return "Recorded."

    await worker.send(
        f"Task:\n\n{spec}\n\n"
        "When done, call finish(summary). If impossible, "
        "call give_up(reason)."
    )
    # wait for the done/fail lifecycle triggered by the agent events
    return await wait()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(asyncio.run(run_task("Write 10 diverse haikus about git rebase.")))"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">asyncio</span>

    <span class="pl-c"># register tools the agent can call in-harness</span>
    <span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">worker</span>.<span class="pl-c1">on</span>(<span class="pl-s">"finish"</span>)</span>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Core concepts</h2><a id="user-content-core-concepts" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Core concepts" href="#core-concepts"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Agent processes</h3><a id="user-content-agent-processes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Agent processes" href="#agent-processes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The central object of ramure is the <code>agent_process</code> (AP), defined by decorating an async function with <code>@agent_process</code>. Inside the function, you define agents and machines as well as how they should communicate.</p>
<p dir="auto">When a root AP gets called, ramure initializes a runtime that is responsible for the lifecycle of the agents and machines it owns. Nested APs inherit the active runtime. To control the lifecycle of an AP, you define events that agents can call back into deterministic Python through <code>@agent.on(...)</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Structuring how information moves in your program makes it easier to reliably use agent labor, especially in more complex cases. You can also configure which <code>image</code> an AP runs from — your local machine by default, or any other backend (see <a href="#images-and-machines">Images and machines</a>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Composition</h3><a id="user-content-composition" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Composition" href="#composition"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">APs compose. An AP can call another AP the way you'd call any async function:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@agent_process
async def main():
    code = await write_code("fibonacci function")
    review = await review_code(code)
    return code"><pre><span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">agent_process</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">main</span>():
    <span class="pl-s1">code</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">write_code</span>(<span class="pl-s">"fibonacci function"</span>)
    <span class="pl-s1">review</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">review_code</span>(<span class="pl-s1">code</span>)
    <span class="pl-k">return</span> <span class="pl-s1">code</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Or fan out concurrently with <code>asyncio.gather</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@agent_process
async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        research("Rust"),
        research("Python"),
    )
    return results"><pre><span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">agent_process</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">main</span>():
    <span class="pl-s1">results</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">asyncio</span>.<span class="pl-c1">gather</span>(
        <span class="pl-en">research</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Rust"</span>),
        <span class="pl-en">research</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Python"</span>),

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Observation, bubbling, and retry</h3><a id="user-content-observation-bubbling-and-retry" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Observation, bubbling, and retry" href="#observation-bubbling-and-retry"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">An AP can also <code>spawn()</code> and obtain a handle to the running AP whose events become observable in real time.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@agent_process
async def main():
    handle = spawn(flaky_task, "write a haiku")

    async for event in handle.events:
        if event.type == "failed":
            handle = spawn(flaky_task, "write a haiku")
        elif event.type == "done":
            return event.data"><pre><span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">agent_process</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">main</span>():
    <span class="pl-s1">handle</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">spawn</span>(<span class="pl-s1">flaky_task</span>, <span class="pl-s">"write a haiku"</span>)

    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-s1">handle</span>.<span class="pl-c1">events</span>:
        <span class="pl-k">if</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">type</span> <span class="pl-c1">==</span> <span class="pl-s">"failed"</span>:
            <span class="pl-s1">handle</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">spawn</span>(<span class="pl-s1">flaky_task</span>, <span class="pl-s">"write a haiku"</span>)
        <span class="pl-k">elif</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">type</span> <span class="pl-c1">==</span> <span class="pl-s">"done"</span>:
            <span class="pl-k">return</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">data</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This handle holds on to the child AP's event stream, so you can observe it as it runs, retry if it fails, and pass events along to higher-level supervisors using <code>bubble()</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Processes can emit custom events with <code>emit(type, data)</code>. If a supervisor wants child events to appear on its own event stream, use <code>bubble()</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@agent_process
async def worker_pool(specs: list[str]) -> None:
    for i, spec in enumerate(specs):
        tid = f"t{i:04d}"
        bubble(spawn(run_task, tid, spec), source=tid)
    await wait()"><pre><span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">agent_process</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">worker_pool</span>(<span class="pl-s1">specs</span>: <span class="pl-s1">list</span>[<span class="pl-smi">str</span>]) <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-c1">None</span>:
    <span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">i</span>, <span class="pl-s1">spec</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-en">enumerate</span>(<span class="pl-s1">specs</span>):
        <span class="pl-s1">tid</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s">f"t<span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-kos">{</span><span class="pl-s1">i</span>:04d<span class="pl-kos">}</span></span>"</span>
        <span class="pl-en">bubble</span>(<span class="pl-en">spawn</span>(<span class="pl-s1">run_task</span>, <span class="pl-s1">tid</span>, <span class="pl-s1">spec</span>), <span class="pl-s1">source</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">tid</span>)
    <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">wait</span>()</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Now a parent observing <code>spawn(worker_pool, specs).events</code> can see child events too, tagged with <code>source=tid</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Images and machines</h3><a id="user-content-images-and-machines" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Images and machines" href="#images-and-machines"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Where does an agent actually run? In ramure that's the <strong>machine</strong> — a running environment. An <strong>image</strong> is the template that spawns one.</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="Image.spawn() -> Machine"><pre class="notranslate"><code>Image.spawn() -> Machine
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">A <code>Machine</code> is anything that satisfies four async methods:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="class Machine(ABC):
    async def exec(self, command, *, user="agent", timeout=None) -> ExecResult: ...
    async def write_file(self, path, content) -> None: ...
    async def read_file(self, path) -> bytes: ...
    async def stop(self) -> None: ..."><pre><span class="pl-k">class</span> <span class="pl-v">Machine</span>(<span class="pl-c1">ABC</span>):
    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">exec</span>(<span class="pl-s1">self</span>, <span class="pl-s1">command</span>, <span class="pl-c1">*</span>, <span class="pl-s1">user</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"agent"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">timeout</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">None</span>) <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-smi">ExecResult</span>: ...
    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">write_file</span>(<span class="pl-s1">self</span>, <span class="pl-s1">path</span>, <span class="pl-s1">content</span>) <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-c1">None</span>: ...
    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">read_file</span>(<span class="pl-s1">self</span>, <span class="pl-s1">path</span>) <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-smi">bytes</span>: ...
    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">stop</span>(<span class="pl-s1">self</span>) <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-c1">None</span>: ...</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">That's the whole contract. ramure uses <code>exec</code> to launch the <code>pi</code> harness in a tmux session on the machine, <code>write_file</code> to drop the agent extension there, and <code>stop</code> for cleanup. Two optional methods, <code>fork()</code> and <code>snapshot()</code>, let backends expose cheap state duplication if they have it (MorphCloud does; LocalMachine doesn't).</p>
<p dir="auto">Bundled backends:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>LocalImage(workdir=, env=)</code> — your host. Default. Each spawned <code>LocalMachine</code> is just a working directory.</li>
<li><code>DockerImage("image:tag", workdir=, env=, volumes=)</code> — a local Docker container. The image must include <code>bash</code>, <code>tmux</code>, <code>pi</code>, and an <code>agent</code> user. Uses <code>--network host</code> by default so the agent can reach the local runtime. <code>ramure connect</code> / <code>ramure ssh</code> use <code>docker exec -it</code> for Docker agents.</li>
<li><code>MorphImage(...)</code> — <a href="https://morphcloud.com" rel="nofollow">MorphCloud</a> VMs. Snapshot/fork friendly. <code>pip install ramure[morph]</code>.</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Adding your own backend</h3><a id="user-content-adding-your-own-backend" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Adding your own backend" href="#adding-your-own-backend"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A new backend is a pair: an <code>Image</code> that knows how to bring up a machine, and a <code>Machine</code> that wraps the running thing. Pass an instance anywhere ramure takes one: <code>@agent_process(image=MyImage(...))</code>, <code>await agent("name", image=...)</code>, or <code>await machine(image=...)</code>. The runtime takes care of registering the agent over WebSocket from inside the machine, and tears everything down via <code>Machine.stop()</code> when the AP exits.</p>
<p dir="auto">Look at <a href="/fulcrumresearch/ramure/blob/main/ramure/machines/local.py"><code>ramure/machines/local.py</code></a> (~110 lines) for the simplest reference implementation, <a href="/fulcrumresearch/ramure/blob/main/ramure/machines/docker.py"><code>ramure/machines/docker.py</code></a> for a CLI-backed container implementation, and <a href="/fulcrumresearch/ramure/blob/main/ramure/machines/morph.py"><code>ramure/machines/morph.py</code></a> for one with SSH, snapshots, and forking.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Endpoints and afforded interfaces</h3><a id="user-content-endpoints-and-afforded-interfaces" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Endpoints and afforded interfaces" href="#endpoints-and-afforded-interfaces"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">APs can also encode specific ways in which they are interacted with, by exposing an API that can be called in code, or via another agent. To do this, use the <code>@expose</code> decorator:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@agent_process
async def worker_pool() -> None:
    specs: dict[str, str] = {}

    @expose
    async def add_task(spec: str) -> str:
        tid = f"t{len(specs):04d}"
        specs[tid] = spec
        emit("task_added", {"task_id": tid, "spec": spec})
        bubble(spawn(run_task, tid, spec), source=tid)
        return tid

    @expose
    async def tasks() -> dict[str, str]:
        return dict(specs)

    emit("ready", None)
    await wait()"><pre><span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">agent_process</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">worker_pool</span>() <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-c1">None</span>:
    <span class="pl-s1">specs</span>: <span class="pl-s1">dict</span>[<span class="pl-smi">str</span>, <span class="pl-smi">str</span>] <span class="pl-c1">=</span> {}

    <span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">expose</span></span>
    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">add_task</span>(<span class="pl-s1">spec</span>: <span class="pl-smi">str</span>) <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-smi">str</span>:
        <span class="pl-s1">tid</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s">f"t<span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-kos">{</span><span class="pl-en">len</span>(<span class="pl-s1">specs</span>):04d<span class="pl-kos">}</span></span>"</span>
        <span class="pl-s1">specs</span>[<span class="pl-s1">tid</span>] <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">spec</span>
        <span class="pl-en">emit</span>(<span class="pl-s">"task_added"</span>, {<span class="pl-s">"task_id"</span>: <span class="pl-s1">tid</span>, <span class="pl-s">"spec"</span>: <span class="pl-s1">spec</span>})
        <span class="pl-en">bubble</span>(<span class="pl-en">spawn</span>(<span class="pl-s1">run_task</span>, <span class="pl-s1">tid</span>, <span class="pl-s1">spec</span>), <span class="pl-s1">source</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">tid</span>)
        <span class="pl-k">return</span> <span class="pl-s1">tid</span>

    <span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">expose</span></span>
    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">tasks</span>() <span class="pl-c1">-></span> <span class="pl-s1">dict</span>[<span class="pl-smi">str</span>, <span class="pl-smi">str</span>]:
        <span class="pl-k">return</span> <span class="pl-en">dict</span>(<span class="pl-s1">specs</span>)

    <span class="pl-en">emit</span>(<span class="pl-s">"ready"</span>, <span class="pl-c1">None</span>)
    <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">wait</span>()</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">You can then consume the exposed worker pool in various ways:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@agent_process
async def main():
    pool = spawn(worker_pool)

    async for event in pool.events:
        if event.type == "ready":
            break

    # call directly
    await pool.call("add_task", spec="Write a haiku about git rebase.")

    # or attach an agent to call the exposed functions on the pool,
    # which get exposed as tools
    monitor = await agent(
        "monitor",
        system_prompt="You run a pool of workers.",
    )
    await pool.attach(monitor, prefix="pool_")"><pre><span class="pl-en">@<span class="pl-s1">agent_process</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">main</span>():
    <span class="pl-s1">pool</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">spawn</span>(<span class="pl-s1">worker_pool</span>)

    <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-s1">pool</span>.<span class="pl-c1">events</span>:
        <span class="pl-k">if</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">type</span> <span class="pl-c1">==</span> <span class="pl-s">"ready"</span>:
            <span class="pl-k">break</span>

    <span class="pl-c"># call directly</span>
    <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">pool</span>.<span class="pl-c1">call</span>(<span class="pl-s">"add_task"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">spec</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Write a haiku about git rebase."</span>)

    <span class="pl-c"># or attach an agent to call the exposed functions on the pool,</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># which get exposed as tools</span>
    <span class="pl-s1">monitor</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">agent</span>(
        <span class="pl-s">"monitor"</span>,
        <span class="pl-s1">system_prompt</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"You run a pool of workers."</span>,
    )
    <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">pool</span>.<span class="pl-c1">attach</span>(<span class="pl-s1">monitor</span>, <span class="pl-s1">prefix</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"pool_"</span>)</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This lets you give a component narrow affordances instead of ambient access to everything. Endpoints run inside the child process's scope, so calls to <code>emit()</code>, <code>done()</code>, and <code>fail()</code> inside an endpoint affect the child, not the caller. Child-owned agents are also visible through <code>handle.agents</code> once the child has created them.</p>

<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>await agent(name, system_prompt=, model=, image=, machine=)</code> — create an agent (<code>model</code> is passed to pi's <code>--model</code>)</li>
<li><code>await machine(image=)</code> — spawn a standalone machine</li>

<li><code>fail(reason)</code> — signal process failure</li>

<li><code>bubble(handle, source=)</code> — forward a child process's events onto the current process stream</li>

<p dir="auto">Running a root <code>@agent_process</code> opens a Unix socket at
<code>~/.ramure/runtimes/{execution_id}.sock</code> and writes a per-run log tree
under <code>~/.ramure/logs/{execution_id}/</code>. The <code>ramure</code> CLI uses these:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="ramure ls                                       # live runs
ramure status [--id <prefix>]                   # agents, machines, connections, affordances
ramure send <agent> <msg> [--id <prefix>]
ramure call <endpoint> [k=v ...] [--id <prefix>] [--json]   # invoke an @expose'd endpoint
ramure connect <agent> [--id <prefix>]          # tmux attach
ramure ssh <agent> [--id <prefix>]              # shell on the agent's machine"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>ramure ls                                       # live runs
ramure status [--id <prefix>]                   # agents, machines, connections, affordances
ramure send <agent> <msg> [--id <prefix>]
ramure call <endpoint> [k=v ...] [--id <prefix>] [--json]   # invoke an @expose'd endpoint
ramure connect <agent> [--id <prefix>]          # tmux attach
ramure ssh <agent> [--id <prefix>]              # shell on the agent's machine
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>--id</code> takes an execution-id prefix. Omit it when there's only one live run.
All commands require the run to be live (socket present). Finished-run logs
remain under <code>~/.ramure/logs/{execution_id}/</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agent logs include raw activity events from <code>pi</code>. Assistant responses also emit
<code>usage</code> entries with token counts and estimated cost; those entries are mirrored
into <code>_runtime.jsonl</code> with an <code>agent</code> field for run-level accounting.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto"><code>ramure call</code> and external affordances</h3><a id="user-content-ramure-call-and-external-affordances" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: ramure call and external affordances" href="#ramure-call-and-external-affordances"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Whatever the root <code>@agent_process</code> <code>@expose</code>s is reachable from outside
the program via <code>ramure call</code>. Arguments are parsed as JSON first, with
string fallback, so typed values work without flags:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="ramure call add_task spec="write tests"
ramure call add_task count=3 enabled=true tags='["a","b"]'
ramure call list_tasks --json"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>ramure call add_task spec="write tests"
ramure call add_task count=3 enabled=true tags='["a","b"]'
ramure call list_tasks --json
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Nested AP <code>@expose</code>s remain internal — reach them via <code>handle.call</code> /
<code>handle.attach</code> from owning code. Only the root program's surface is
externally addressable.</p>
